hero.h1:
Scams look real.
Until you look closer.
hero.lead: Paste a suspicious link, SMS, WhatsApp message or screenshot. PhishGuard shows you a risk score, and the exact reasons behind it, in plain words.
hero.xray_aria: The web address http://hdfc-bank-verify.click/login with the lookalike part, hyphen bank hyphen verify dot click, underlined in red and tagged as a lookalike of HDFC Bank.
story.1.p: It looks like it’s from your bank. The sender name is right. The tone is calm and official. Nothing seems wrong yet.
story.2.p: “Blocked today.” “Update now.” Scammers rush you on purpose. A frightened person doesn’t stop to check.
story.3.p: Real bank: hdfcbank.com. This one: hdfc-bank-verify.click. A few extra words and a strange ending is all it takes to fool a hurried eye.
story.4.p: It checks the lookalike domain, the risky ending, the pressure language, and live blocklists. In about a second, every red flag is on the table.
story.5.p: No password typed, no OTP shared, no money moved. That is the whole point: seeing it before you click.
story.stage_aria: Animated illustration. A phone receives a fake bank text with a link. The link is compared with the real bank domain, PhishGuard scans it, shows a risk score of 91 out of 100 with four red flags, stamps it Likely a Scam, and the message is deleted.

faq.1.q: Can PhishGuard guarantee a link is safe?
faq.1.a: No tool can. “Looks safe” means we found no strong warning signs. Brand-new scam sites may not be on any list yet, so never enter passwords or OTPs on a site you reached through a message. Type the official address yourself.
faq.2.q: Is my data stored or sold?
faq.2.a: No. Nothing you paste is stored, logged or sold, and there are no accounts. This site sets no cookies and loads nothing from third parties.
faq.2.a_opt: No. Nothing you paste is stored, logged or sold, and there are no accounts. Analytics cookies are off unless you click Accept in the cookie banner.
faq.3.a: Our server opens the link for you, follows redirects, and reads the page without running its code, looking for fake login forms and hidden redirects. The website sees our server, not you. You can turn it off.
faq.4.q: What does the Deep scan do?
faq.4.a: It looks up how old the domain is and reads the website’s security certificate. Scam sites are very often only days old. It is slower, so it is optional.
faq.5.a: On our held-out test it flags about 73% of real phishing at “Be careful” with about 6.5% false alarms, and 98% precision at “Likely a scam”. Roughly 1 in 4 phishing links still slips through, and the limits of the test are published.
faq.6.q: Does it work for messages in Hindi or other languages?
faq.6.a: Link checks work in any language. The message scanner understands English, Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Spanish and “Hinglish” (Hindi typed in English letters). Scam messages in other languages may be missed, and the non-English rules have had far less testing than the English ones.
faq.7.q: I already sent money or an OTP. What now?
faq.7.a: Call your bank immediately to block the transaction, change your passwords, and report it. In India call 1930 and file at cybercrime.gov.in.
faq.8.a: Yes. It shows no advertising and does not sell data. If that ever changes, we will say so first.

js.safe_s: No strong scam signals found. Still, only enter passwords on sites you reached by typing the address yourself.
js.warn_s: Several warning signs. Don’t enter personal details or payments until you verify through the official website or app.
js.bad_s: Strong phishing/scam indicators. Do not click, reply, or share any code. Delete it and report it.
js.error: Something went wrong. Is the server running?
js.not_inspected: Page not inspected: {err}. That is not a sign of safety: scam sites often block scanners or vanish within hours.
js.no_phrases: No scam phrases detected in the text.
f.no_https.d: The link uses plain HTTP, so anything you type can be intercepted.
f.uses_https.d: Encrypted connection (note: scammers use HTTPS too, so this alone is not proof of safety).
f.ip_host.t: IP address instead of a domain
f.ip_host.d: Legitimate services almost never ask you to log in on a raw IP address.
f.mixed_script.d: The domain mixes alphabets (e.g. Latin + Cyrillic) so letters imitate real ones.
f.idn.d: Uses non-English characters. Common for legitimate sites too, so only a weak signal.
f.free_host.t: Hosted on a free site-builder platform
f.free_host.d: Anyone can create a page on {host} in minutes; scammers abuse it. A real company login would use its own domain.
f.at_trick.d: Everything before '@' is ignored by browsers, a classic trick to disguise the real destination.
f.shortener.d: The real destination is hidden. Expand the link before opening.
f.risky_tld.d: This extension is heavily abused for throwaway scam sites.
f.subdomains.d: {n} subdomain levels. Scammers bury a brand name in front of the real domain.
f.hyphens.d: Domains like 'secure-login-bank-verify' are typical of phishing.
f.long_url.d: {n} characters, long URLs often hide the real destination.
f.digits.d: Randomly generated domains often contain long number strings.
f.impersonates.d: {brand} appears in the address, but the real site is {real}.
f.typosquat.d: '{label}' looks like {brand} with a small change.
f.redirect_param.d: The link forwards you to a different address.
f.new_domain.d: Registered only {d} days ago. Most phishing sites live less than a month.
f.dns_block.d: Cloudflare’s security DNS blocks this domain as malware/phishing.
f.openphish.d: Listed in the OpenPhish live phishing feed.
f.ml.t: AI model: hostname resembles known phishing sites
f.ml.d: A model trained on real phishing data rates this web address {p}% similar to phishing hosts.
f.page_pw.d: Normal on real login pages, so it only matters together with the other signs here.
f.page_otp.t: Page asks for OTP / card / ID details
f.page_otp.d: Fields detected: {f}. Real services never ask for these on a page opened from a message.
f.exfil_form.t: Form sends data to Telegram/Discord/form service
f.exfil_form.d: Stolen details are delivered straight to the scammer’s chat. Legitimate sites never do this.
f.cross_post.t: Login form posts to a different website
f.cross_post.d: Typed details would be sent to {h}, not to this site.
f.insecure_form.d: The form submits over plain HTTP.
f.exfil_script.d: A script on the page posts to a chat webhook, a common phishing-kit trick.
f.title_brand.t: Page title names {brand} but the site isn’t {brand}
f.hidden_iframe.d: An invisible frame loads content from an unfamiliar website.
f.obfuscated.d: The page hides its code (eval/atob/escape chains) so reviewers can’t read it.
f.blocks.d: Phishing kits often disable these to stop victims inspecting or pasting.
f.meta_redirect.d: A meta-refresh sends visitors to another website.
f.nocontent.d: A bare form with very little text is typical of a throwaway phishing page.
f.long_chain.d: {n} redirects before the real page: a way to dodge filters.
f.shortened_safe.d: It leads to {h}, which has no strong warning signs.
f.redirect_bad.d: The link really goes to {h}, which scores {n}/100.
f.t_caps.d: Shouting text is a pressure tactic.
f.t_call.t: Asks you to call/WhatsApp a number
f.t_call.d: Scammers move victims off official channels.
f.e_nodns: domain does not resolve (it may already be taken down)
f.e_connect: could not connect (site down, or it blocks automated visitors)
